req.title: Health probe returns liveness
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /health/ with HTTP 200 and a status:'ok' JSON body.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /health/ returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing status:'ok'. To achieve high mutation kill rate we need: (1) a positive test asserting exact status code 200 AND exact JSON body {'status':'ok'}, (2) a negative test verifying that an unsupported method (POST) returns 405 not 200, and (3) a boundary test verifying the Content-Type header is application/json and that the body key is exactly 'status' with value exactly 'ok' (not 'OK', not 'okay'). Each test uses exact-value assertions to catch constant-mutation, operator-flip, and string-mutation operators.

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_get_returns_200_and_status_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body == {"status": "ok"}
    assert body["status"] == "ok"

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_post_returns_405_not_200():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 405
    assert response.status_code != 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body.get("status") != "ok"

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_response_body_exact_key_and_value():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    content_type = response.headers.get("content-type", "")
    assert "application/json" in content_type
    body = response.json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    assert list(body.keys()) == ["status"]
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert body["status"] != "OK"
    assert body["status"] != "okay"
    assert body["status"] != True
    assert body["status"] != 1
